To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mitochondrial calcium uniporter is encoded by the mitochondrial genome and is composed of two proteins: the MCU and a regulatory protein, the mitochondrial calcium uptake 1 (MICU1).

(1) Trypanosomes are the first eukaryotes to be shown to possess a mitochondrial calcium uniport system; (2) The trypanosome mitochondrial calcium uniporter is a member of the mitochondrial carrier family; and (3) The trypanosomal uniporter is the first member of a new subfamily of mitochondrial carriers that includes the vertebrate uniporter and a yeast mitochondrial protein that is essential for the maintenance of mitochondrial DNA.
a protein that is essential for mitochondrial Ca(2+) uptake in trypanosomes is also present in mammals, and that this protein is the mitochondrial calcium uniporter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the mitochondrial calcium transport and its regulation, and the identification and characterization of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter protein.
the molecular biology and biochemistry of the mitochondrion and its role in cell physiology and disease.
the molecular basis of the trypanosomal cell cycle and the cell cycle-dependent regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trypanosomes have contributed to the identification of a new protein that is essential for the uptake of calcium into mitochondria and is involved in the regulation of cellular calcium levels.
trypanosomes have contributed to our knowledge of mitochondrial Ca(2+) uptake by providing a model system for the discovery and characterization of the MCU.
trypanosomes have provided a solution to a 40-year mitochondrial calcium mystery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the trypanosome mitochondrion is a unique system for studying mitochondrial calcium transport and its role in cell physiology and death, and that trypanosomes are a unique system for investigating mitochondrial structure and function.
the study of the biology of trypanosomatid organisms has contributed to our understanding of the biology of mammals.
the trypanosome mitochondrial genome has a single gene, cox1, encoding a polypeptide that is homologous to the N-terminal portion of the mammalian cytochrome c oxidase subunit I.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trypanosomes are a good source of proteins for mammalian biochemistry and cell biology.
trypanosomes are an excellent source of information for the study of mitochondrial functions in mammalian cells.
a mitochondrial Ca(2+) uniporter is essential for the survival of vertebrate and trypanosome cells, but not of yeast cells.
